subject.title: feat(hooks): emit session prune lifecycle event

question: Should `session:prune` expose only bounded sanitized metadata from the active pruning path, or should OpenClaw support richer pruned-content data for hook consumers?
rationale: The implementation choice sets the privacy, compatibility, and latency contract for hook handlers in the context-building path, and the current PR mixes unbounded await semantics with raw tool metadata.

options.title: Metadata-only active-path hook
options.body: Port the hook to `agent-hooks`, emit counts/timestamp/session identity and sanitized bounded tool metadata only, and keep handler delivery bounded or fire-and-forget.

options.title: Trusted raw-content opt-in
options.body: Allow pruned content only behind an explicit trusted opt-in after documenting privacy, size, timeout, and logging expectations.

options.title: Pause for broader memory design
options.body: Defer this PR until reset, prune, and compaction memory hooks are designed together with a single contract.

recommendation.title: Metadata-only active-path hook
recommendation.body: Port the hook to `agent-hooks`, emit counts/timestamp/session identity and sanitized bounded tool metadata only, and keep handler delivery bounded or fire-and-forget.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent owns the current implementation attempt and has adjacent hook-surface history, making him the best routing candidate for the hook contract choice.
